scale.1: Strong concern: significant gaps; would not pass this dimension at the target level.
scale.2: Below bar: partially demonstrated, relied on the AI without judgement, or had notable errors.
scale.3: At bar: solid, with minor gaps; meets FAANG mid/senior expectations for AI-assisted work.
scale.4: Above bar: exceptional; used the AI as a force multiplier while clearly owning the solution.

dimensions.name: Problem understanding & framing
dimensions.signals: Understood the problem themselves before delegating: clarified inputs, constraints and edge cases with the interviewer; chose (or at least evaluated) the approach rather than adopting whatever the AI proposed; broke the work into pieces suited to delegation.

levels.1: Pasted the problem into the AI and adopted its answer without engaging with the problem.
levels.2: Some understanding, but the AI framed the problem and picked the approach without scrutiny.
levels.3: Clarified the problem, picked or validated a sound approach, and delegated well-scoped pieces.
levels.4: Framed the problem crisply, compared approaches, and steered the AI toward the best one from the start.

dimensions.name: Directing the AI
dimensions.signals: Prompts were specific and gave the needed context (constraints, signature, edge cases, the code in question); asked for what they actually needed; iterated when the answer was off; used the AI for the right tasks (boilerplate, recall, review, test ideas) rather than for thinking they should do themselves; respected the time box.

levels.1: Vague or copy-paste prompts; repeated the same request; got little useful from the AI or lost a lot of time to it.
levels.2: Usable prompts that often lacked context, needing several round trips; unclear what they wanted from the AI.
levels.3: Clear, context-rich prompts; targeted asks; corrected course efficiently when an answer missed.
levels.4: Precise, well-sequenced prompts that got high-value help on the first try, including asking the AI to critique or test its own output.

dimensions.name: Verifying AI output
dimensions.signals: Read AI-written code before adopting it; ran tests and added custom inputs that target risky logic; caught AI mistakes (wrong edge cases, wrong complexity, invented APIs, misread requirements); asked follow-up questions when something looked off; never assumed AI output was correct.

levels.1: Accepted AI output blindly; submitted AI code without running or reading it, or missed obvious AI errors.
levels.2: Ran the sample tests but did little else to check AI output; some AI mistakes slipped through.
levels.3: Reviewed and tested AI output deliberately and caught the mistakes that mattered.
levels.4: Systematically verified every adopted piece with targeted tests and reasoning, and caught subtle AI errors.

dimensions.name: Understanding & ownership
dimensions.signals: Could explain every part of the final code, including AI-written parts, and its complexity; adapted AI code deliberately to the problem and their style; answered the interviewer's and the written follow-up questions without leaning on the AI.

levels.1: Couldn't explain the code they submitted or its complexity.
levels.2: Explained the gist but was shaky on the details or the complexity of the AI-written parts.
levels.3: Explained the full solution and its complexity confidently, and adapted AI code where needed.
levels.4: Deep command of the solution: improved on the AI's code, and reasoned about alternatives and limits.

dimensions.name: Final correctness & code quality
dimensions.signals: The final code passes the hidden tests, handles edge cases, has the expected complexity, and is clean and readable, regardless of who wrote which line.

levels.1: Fails most tests or doesn't run.
levels.2: Partially correct, or correct but inefficient or messy.
levels.3: Correct on nearly all tests with the expected complexity; clean code.
levels.4: Fully correct, optimal, and production quality.

dimensions.name: Communication
dimensions.signals: Kept the interviewer informed about what they were asking the AI and why, and what they concluded from its answers; explained decisions; follow-up answers were clear.

levels.1: Worked silently with the AI; the interviewer couldn't follow what was happening.
levels.2: Occasional narration; decisions about AI output were mostly unexplained.
levels.3: Narrated the plan and the AI's role clearly, and explained what they accepted or rejected.
levels.4: Exceptionally clear: treated the interviewer as a collaborator, and the reasoning behind every AI decision was visible.
